title: Mariners sending prized rookie shortstop Colt Emerson to minors, AP source says
description: Seattle Mariners rookie shortstop Colt Emerson will be optioned to Triple-A Tacoma before Friday night's game against the Houston Astros, a person with knowledge of the situation told The Associated Press on Thursday.  Emerson is hitting .190 with eight homers and 23 RBIs in 69 games.  The 21-year-old will be replaced on the roster by utilityman Brock Rodden, who was hitting .262 with 19 homers and 65 RBIs in 92 Triple-A games.
fullText:
SEATTLE (AP) — Seattle Mariners rookie shortstop Colt Emerson will be optioned to Triple-A Tacoma before Friday night's game against the Houston Astros, a person with knowledge of the situation told The Associated Press on Thursday.

The person spoke to the AP on condition of anonymity because the transaction was not official.

Emerson is hitting .190 with eight homers and 23 RBIs in 69 games. The 21-year-old will be replaced on the roster by utilityman Brock Rodden, who was hitting .262 with 19 homers and 65 RBIs in 92 Triple-A games.

Emerson signed a $95 million, eight-year contract on April 1 — the biggest commitment at the time for a player who had yet to appear in the big leagues. In May, he became the youngest Mariners player to make his major league debut since Félix Hernández, who was 19 on Aug. 4, 2005.

The rookie's struggles at the plate have only intensified recently. In August, Emerson hit .182 with one homer, two RBIs and 14 strikeouts in 33 at-bats.

The Mariners are 57-65 after beating the New York Yankees 1-0 on Thursday to snap a six-game skid. Seattle won the AL West and reached the AL Championship Series last season.

title: Yankees' Carlos Rodon strikes out seven in potential final rehab start
description: Yankees left-hander Carlos Rodon followed up a strong first rehab start with a gem on Thursday night, pitching 4.1 scoreless innings and striking out seven batters for Double-A Somerset.
fullText:
Carlos Rodon followed up a strong first rehab start with a gem on Thursday night.

Pitching for Double-A Somerset, the Yankees southpaw tossed 4.1 shutout innings and allowed two hits and one walk while striking out seven batters.

After a delayed start due to inclement weather, Rodon took the mound and allowed a bloop single to lead off the game. Rodon bounced back, getting a fly out and an inning-ending double play to end the first frame.

Rodon then came out in the second, striking out two in a 1-2-3 inning. After Somerset put up a four-spot in the bottom half of the second, Rodon worked around a leadoff single by striking out the next three batters to keep New Hampshire off the board. Rodon struck out two more batters in the fourth before issuing his first walk to lead off the fifth inning. After picking up an out, Rodon was pulled in the middle of an at-bat after 58 pitches (41 strikes).

Tyler Boudreau came in to finish up the at-bat Rodon left for and got the third out without allowing Rodon's runner to score, putting an end to the veteran's night.

In his last rehab start, Rodon struck out four batters while allowing three runs on three hits and two walks across 2.2 innings. Thursday's start was a stark improvement as Rodon continues to build up his pitch count.

Earlier this week, Yankees manager Aaron Boone said this could be Rodon's final rehab start before rejoining the team. If Rodon feels good after Thursday's start, he can be activated next week, even with the limited pitch count. Boone actually stated that Rodon could continue to build up his count while pitching in a piggyback situation.

That could be a temporary solution for the upcoming rotation crunch that will befall the Yankees. When Rodon is ready to start games, New York will have to decide which of Will Warren or Ryan Weathers will be added to the bullpen.

title: Utah State guard Kolby King announces Auburn basketball commitment
description: Fifth-year guard Kolby King announced his commitment to Auburn basketball on Thursday, becoming a late addition thanks to a recent court ruling.
fullText:
AUBURN — With its season just months away, Auburn basketball is apparently making a late roster addition thanks to a recent court ruling.

Utah State guard Kolby King — a fifth-year who was granted an additional year of eligibility due to a lawsuit in Ohio — announced his commitment to the program on his personal Instagram account on Thursday, Aug. 13, making Auburn his fifth school in as many seasons.

King was among one of at least 15 plaintiffs in a lawsuit filed in June, which led to a preliminary injunction granting eligibility for the 2026-27 season. Prior to Auburn, King spent his senior year with Utah State. He began his career at St. John's, and he spilt his following two seasons between Tulane and Butler, respectively.

As a depth piece for the Aggies, King played in 36 games but he never made a start. He did average 19.2 minutes off the bench, and he also averaged 7.5 points and 3.3 rebounds while shooting a career-high 47.7% from the floor. He also shot 39.3% from 3-point range.

That's now nine additions to Auburn's roster as the program heads into its second season under head coach Steven Pearl. The program returned Tahaad Pettiford and Kevin Overton, as well as Simon Walker and Blake Muschalek, but it added five transfers and made three signings; one from the high-school ranks and two international.

title: Former Eagles Pass Rusher Eyes NFL Return After Unretirement Decision
description: One of the Philadelphia Eagles old friends has made an unexpected decision regarding his football future. The post Former Eagles Pass Rusher Eyes NFL Return After Unretirement Decision appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
The Philadelphia Eagles are entering what feels like a very important season in 2026. After a wild card exit in the playoffs last year, the Eagles need to make a deeper playoff run in order to keep their fans and the front office happy. While there's still a lot of work to be done between now and the start of the regular season, Philly has put together some solid work early on in training camp.

One of the team's biggest goals this offseason involved finding some help in the pass rush department, which led to the acquisition of Jonathan Greenard in a trade with the Minnesota Vikings. As folks will remember from last year, one of the team's top pass rushers, Za'Darius Smith, opted to retire from football early in the year, but after surprisingly deciding to unretire, he has taken a big step towards making his return to the NFL.

A fourth-round pick in the 2015 NFL Draft, Smith made a career for himself as a pass-rush specialist, spending time with several different teams. Along the way, he's earned three Pro Bowl selections and a spot on the All-Pro Second Team in 2020, which was the best season of his career (52 tackles, 12.5 sacks, two pass breakups, four forced fumbles).

Smith latched on with the Eagles right before the start of the 2025 campaign, but his usage patterns immediately raised concerns. While he picked up 10 tackles and 1.5 sacks in five games, Smith decided to retire in October, leaving Philadelphia in a tough spot when it came to finding players who could get after the quarterback.

The front office managed to address that need this offseason, but it will surely be intrigued to see that Smith is planning a return to the NFL. Reports emerged on Thursday afternoon indicating that, now that he has officially unretired, Smith is taking a free agent visit with one of his former teams, the Cleveland Browns.

"Free agent pass-rusher Za'Darius Smith, who recently un-retired with the possibility of playing, worked out for the Browns today," Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reported in a post on X.

GettyPhiladelphia Eagles edge rusher Za'Darius Smith.

Considering how Smith's time with the Eagles unfolded, he probably isn't remembered too fondly by fans, as he left the team in a tough spot when he decided to retire. That's just how the cookie crumbles sometimes, though, and with Greenard in tow now, you can make an argument that the pass rush is significantly improved (assuming he can stay healthy, of course).

There's no guarantee Smith will be returning to the NFL, but he seems intent on finding his way back ahead of the 2026 campaign. A return to the Eagles almost certainly will not happen, but several other teams are expected to show interest in him alongside the Browns, and given his ties to Philly, fans will likely be keeping close tabs on his status as he attempts to find his way back into the league.

title: Sabres Grades: Young Forward Quinn Took Sizeable Step Forward In 2025-26, But Buffalo Still Needs More Out Of Him
description: TheHockeyNews.com's series handing out grades for Buffalo Sabres players this past season – and in this file in the series, we're focusing on Sabres forward Jack Quinn. He took a major step forward in 2025-26, but should Buffalo fans expect more out of Quinn?
fullText:
The Buffalo Sabres finally made it into the Stanley Cup playoffs this past season after a 15-year absence, skyrocketing to the top of the Atlantic Division, beating the Boston Bruins in Round 1 of the post-season, then losing to the Montreal Canadiens in the second round .

So, while the ending to their season wasn't ideal, the Sabres' growth last season means TheHockeyNews.com's annual grades for Sabres players will be positive. You'd need a perfect year to get an A+ grade, but you also won't see Buffalo's players get a failing or sub-par grade.

In this "Sabres Grades" file, we're turning the spotlight on up-and-coming winger Jack Quinn. The 24-year-old had a career-best season on offense last year, and he'll be an RFA after this coming season. Buffalo needs continued growth from Quinn, and he's got every motivation to have a strong 2026-27 season

The Skinny: For the first three seasons of Quinn's NHL career, he was finding his footing. In his rookie year, he posted 14 goals and 37 points in 75 games. Then, in his sophomore year of 2023-24, Quinn had to deal with injuries limiting him to 27 games – but he still produced 10 assists and 19 points in that span. And in 2024-25, Quinn produced 15 goals and 39 points in 74 games. His trajectory was still going the right way.

The Sabres needed more from Quinn in 2025-26, and 'more' is exactly what Buffalo got from Quinn last season, as he posted 20 goals and 51 points in 82 games in Year 1 of a two-year contract paying him the bargain rate of $3.375-million per-season. And in Buffalo's playoffs this spring, Quinn posted five assists and seven points in 13 games. That's not outstanding, but it's definitely encouraging.

Buffalo has Quinn slotting in on their second line of forwards, and while that's a position that's going to give him terrific opportunities, it also carries with it considerable pressure to perform. So, while Quinn and the Sabres should be thrilled with Quinn's performance last season, Buffalo also needs Quinn to take additional steps to graduate to a higher echelon – something that's been envisioned for him since Quinn was drafted eighth-overall in 2020.

Quinn doesn't have to put the Sabres on his back to earn an A+ grade from this writer. But you'd like to see Quinn's plus/minus be better than the plus-4 he posted last season – by comparison, teammate Ryan McLeod was a plus-25 – and yes, you'd absolutely like to see an improvement with Quinn's totals on offense.

The Sabres need overall improvement to go further in the post-season next spring, but Quinn is going to be a key component for them. He took an important step forward in '25-26, but Quinn has to show (a) there are still levels he can ascend to; and (b) he has to do so with some semblance of consistency.

If Quinn thrives this coming season, he's going to put the Sabres in a delicate situation. At that point, we'll have to see what road Sabres GM Jarmo Kekalainen chooses with Quinn – a lengthy contract extension, or a shorter 'bridge' deal. The stakes are sky-high for Quinn, but Buffalo fans have seen enough out of him to feel confident he can grow his game and develop into the first-rate NHLer the Sabres want and need him to be.

title: Kevin Durant congratulates 'inspiring' Russell Westbrook on retirement
description: Kevin Durant and Russell Westbrook spent eight years together on the Thunder. Durant shared a heartfelt message about Westbrook's retirement.
fullText:
Kevin Durant is a future Hall of Famer himself, but upon hearing the news of Russell Westbrook's retirement, he called his former Oklahoma City Thunder teammate "inspiring."

A day after Westbrook announced he's bidding adieu to basketball, Durant took to X on Thursday, Aug. 13 to write a heartfelt post to the point guard, who played 18 seasons in the NBA. The duo spent eight years together early in their NBA careers. They took Oklahoma City, which moved from Seattle the summer Westbrook joined the team, to the playoffs five times. They reached the Finals in the 2011-12 season, where they lost to LeBron James and the Miami Heat.

In his reflection, Durant gave insight into who Westbrook is as a player and person.

"A lot of people looked at the emotions on the court and thought Russ was loud, nah to me, he was quiet and methodical," Durant said. "He lead by example and once the lights were bright, he let everything out and experienced pure freedom. It was inspiring as his teammate and everywhere I went, I seen it inspire people from all walks of life, crazy thing is, he didn't say much, he just showed up."

Durant is a 16-time All-Star and won two championships after leaving the Thunder in 2016. Westbrook was named an All-Star nine times and became the NBA's triple-double king upon his own departure from Oklahoma City in 2019. They played together during the 2016 NBA All-Star Game when Westbrook was named MVP.

The Slim Reaper recalled how he and the former UCLA standout developed a friendship. He said they encouraged each other through the highs and lows of their careers and the everyday moments, "bus rides, plane rides, card games, jokes and arguments," and concluded, "the whole thing, memorable!!"

Durant shared a story of when he asked Thunder assistant coach Maurice Cheeks if it's harder to work out before or after practice because he saw Westbrook coming in to train before. When he remembered Cheeks saying, "coming in before practice is probably harder," Durant took on the challenge that his point guard set the tone with, saying "since then, it's been my routine."

Durant reflected on the exclusive nature of being an NBA player and the understanding he and Westbrook have for each other and the game. He expressed hope that his teammate will continue his legacy, calling his career "iconic."

"This basketball life is sacred to us as professionals, what we put into that court means everything," he said. "Some of us wish we could go back and do things with a little more intent and some can just wipe their hands and be satisfied with the time spent. Who u gonna be? We know what zero was on … keep inspiring in the next phase of life champ. ... much love and Congratulations on a iconic career."

title: Saints' Etienne is still popular with ex-Jags teammates, touts Tuten's potential with Jacksonville
description: New Orleans running back Travis Etienne Jr. and Jacksonville quarterback Trevor Lawrence greeted one another warmly near the middle of a practice field at Saints headquarters, catching up and posing for photos after their teams finished a joint practice on Thursday.  From 2018 until this year, they'd known each other only as teammates — first at Clemson and then with the Jaguars, who drafted both in 2021.
fullText:
METAIRIE, La. (AP) — New Orleans running back Travis Etienne Jr. and Jacksonville quarterback Trevor Lawrence greeted one another warmly near the middle of a practice field at Saints headquarters, catching up and posing for photos after their teams finished a joint practice on Thursday.

From 2018 until this year, they'd known each other only as teammates — first at Clemson and then with the Jaguars, who drafted both in 2021.

That changed in March, when the Saints lured Etienne back to his native Louisiana with a four-year contract worth up to $52 million.

Still, Etienne was in high demand by former Jaguars teammates, coaches and other staff who looked eager to say hello and wish him well.

"It was great to see him after practice," Jaguars second-year coach Liam Coen said. "We'll never be able to replace what he was able to do for us, whether it was last year or what he's done in Jacksonville throughout the course of his career."

For Etienne "to come back home and to play for an organization which he, I know, followed as a kid and to be able to provide and to get a contract like that, I mean, he should be extremely proud of himself," Coen said. "I am of him — and the relationship that he had with a lot of guys on our team."

Etienne surpassed the 1,000-yard mark as a rusher in three of the past four seasons. In 2025, he rushed for 1,107 yards and seven touchdowns, and also had 292 yards receiving and six TD catches.

Bhayshul Tuten — who is among the leading candidates to become Jacksonville's No. 1 running back this season — said Etienne will bring more than production on the field to the Saints.

Etienne was adept at helping younger Jaguars teammates understand the play book and at demonstrating how to take a professional approach to football, said Tuten, a 2025 fourth-round draft choice out of Virginia Tech.

"He was always in the treatment room. He was always getting something done. If he wasn't hurt, if he wasn't nicked up, he'd still be in there just doing the preventative things," Tuten said. "He's a great guy and I'm definitely grateful I met him."

Tuten said he and Etienne bonded over their enjoyment of high-performance cars. They drive similar makes and models (M series BMWs) and enjoy customizing them with accessories. Tuten credits time spent with Etienne on and off the field with preparing him to take on a larger role in Jacksonville's backfield.

"Being with him for a year, and then one of your good pals goes off and now he's in New Orleans, it's sad to see," Tuten said. "But I know he got what he deserved and he's happy.

"Now my role increases more, which I'm excited for," Tuten added. "So it's a little sour, but a little sweet at the same time."

Etienne beamed when he spoke about being able to catch up with the Jaguars.

"It's very gratifying," Etienne said. "When you're somewhere at a place for five years and you put your heart and soul into a place, man, that's how it's supposed to be."

Etienne also projected success for Tuten, saying he was proud "to see the growth that he's continued to showcase."

"Even when he was a rookie, he was kind of beyond his years in the way that he prepared and the way he attacked the game," Etienne said. "He always was a sponge; he always was learning.

"He has that work ethic within him to get him to that next level," Etienne added. "That's what's going to make him great."

title: Analysis: Fox News ran 206 WNBA segments this summer
description: On June 24, the Indiana Fever and Phoenix Mercury met for the second time in three days. Both games fed Fox News’ WNBA content machine. During the Fever’s win on June 22, tensions flared, resulting in one chaotic scrum, one ejection, one Sophie Cunningham meme, and five technical fouls. During the Mercury’s win on June…
fullText:
On June 24, the Indiana Fever and Phoenix Mercury met for the second time in three days. Both games fed Fox News' WNBA content machine.

During the Fever's win on June 22, tensions flared, resulting in one chaotic scrum, one ejection, one Sophie Cunningham meme, and five technical fouls.

During the Mercury's win on June 24, Phoenix All-Star forward Alyssa Thomas' fist made contact with Fever All-Star guard Caitlin Clark's throat. The WNBA retroactively levied a one-game suspension against Thomas for "recklessly making contact with her fist to the throat area" of Clark.

Thomas later disclosed that she and her teammates received death threats and racial slurs. Fever head coach Stephanie White and Clark condemned the vitriolic aftermath, as did several other WNBA figures. Instead of heeding that directive, however, Fox News used the Fever and Mercury's two-game set as a launching pad into a summer of antagonistic WNBA coverage.

Media Matters for America has published a report showing that Fox News has "devoted at least 13 hours and 34 minutes," including at least 206 segments, to WNBA programming since June 25.

Up until Cunningham's comments about barring transgender athletes from women's sports for an ESPN profile published July 21, Fox News almost exclusively discussed "hard fouls" in the WNBA. But from July 21 through Aug. 11, the network's segments have been disproportionately dedicated to anti-trans rhetoric with the WNBA as the backdrop.

Fox News' WNBA segments have sprawled across The Five, The Ingraham Angle, Hannity, and Gutfeld!. But while Laura Ingraham, who apparently has granted selective immunity from her 2018 "shut up and dribble" mandate, seems enthusiastic to diagram hard fouls, not every Fox News host is a willing participant in this peculiar pivot.

"This is week three of The Five covering the WNBA, and I have to say, I'm done," Jesse Watters said on The Five on Aug. 3. "I hate the WNBA. I don't mind women's basketball. My girls play basketball, but I don't want to cover women's basketball. I don't want to be a WNBA analyst. We get paid to have an opinion about everything. And this is something I don't care about."

At least Watters said the quiet part out loud.

Earlier this week, Fever head coach Stephanie White delivered a powerful statement in the face of even more scrutiny over how she handled DiJonai Carrington's Flagrant 2 foul on Cunningham.

"The hate, the fear-mongering, the divisiveness, the stuff that's trying to hijack our league will not win," White said, in part. "It won't win. We are united, we are connected, [and] we will not be divided. Every day, these women put their ass on the line. Every day. When they go low, we go high. Love will win! Grace will win! Humility will win! And kindness will win! I stand by them. I will always stand by them. Everybody else can go to hell."

Will conservative media listen and leave the league alone? History, and the fact that their coverage has never been rooted in WNBA reality, suggests otherwise. Even if there isn't any controversy to mine, the Fox News powers that be will find one. They already have in Enes Kanter and Royce White's disingenuous antics.

title: ‘Dealing With Unfair Judgment and Hate’ – Iga Świątek Delivers Strongly-Worded Speech After Canadian Open Triumph
description: Iga Świątek didn’t hold back as she breathed a sigh of relief after claiming her first title of 2026 at the Canadian Open in Toronto. The Pole ended an 11-month title drought, with her previous triumph coming at the Korea Open in September 2025.
fullText:
Iga Świątek didn't hold back as she breathed a sigh of relief after claiming her first title of 2026 at the Canadian Open in Toronto. The Pole ended an 11-month title drought, with her previous triumph coming at the Korea Open in September 2025.

After facing numerous questions and concerns about her struggles over the past few months, Świątek hit back at her critics and dedicated her latest trophy to those who, like her, have faced hate and unfair judgment.

Świątek staged a phenomenal run to the title, losing just a couple of sets en route. Her path to the final included victories against Sára Bejlek, Viktorija Golubic, Marta Kostyuk, Diana Shnaider, and Elina Svitolina.

In Thursday's summit clash, she eased past World No. 2 Elena Rybakina 6-2, 6-3 in just one hour and 15 minutes. During her champion's speech, Świątek highlighted the significance of the triumph after enduring some particularly difficult moments on the court.

The former World No. 1, who confessed to feeling lost on the court in March, suggested that regaining her form while dealing with relentless public scrutiny made the process especially challenging.

"I'm really happy about this tournament. It means so, so much to me because these past months were not easy. I'm really happy that I kept focusing on growing, changing my game a little bit, improving despite all the opinions that many people have about me every day on the internet, live. It's not easy to deal with all that. So, I'm happy that the reality is different."

The criticism was not limited to Świątek, with her coaching team also facing scrutiny. That included psychologist Daria Abramowicz and Francisco Roig, the former Rafael Nadal mentor she brought on as her coach in April.

"The reality is that I have people that know me so well and people that support me every week, every day. They're here to give their best work and just keep pushing. So thank you to the team that is here. Thank you to Francis, who's probably flying to Cincinnati right now. Sorry that I had to win the first title with you when you weren't here," she said.

Świątek dedicated the triumph to those going through similar circumstances, urging them to tune out the outside noise and never lose faith in themselves.

"And as I said, I want to dedicate this title to everyone who is dealing with unfair judgment and hate. Just keep pushing, keep growing, keep focusing on yourself because you know what's best for you, and always remember what's ahead and what might be possible, so yeah, here we are."

MORE: Elena Rybakina and Iga Świątek's Prize Money After Canadian Open 2026 Final in Toronto

The victory helped Iga Świątek climb a couple of places in the WTA Race, reaching the 10 position. She would now hope to continue her rich vein of form at the ongoing Cincinnati Open, where she is the defending champion.

This article originally appeared on Pro Football Network.

title: Timberwolves’ Kevin Garnett Jersey Retirement Date Emerges With Fitting Opponent
description: Minnesota Timberwolves legend Kevin Garnett’s No. 21 could finally rise into the Target Center rafters against the perfect opponent. The post Timberwolves’ Kevin Garnett Jersey Retirement Date Emerges With Fitting Opponent appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
The long wait to see Kevin Garnett's No. 21 raised into the Target Center rafters may finally have an end date and an opponent worthy of the occasion.

Timberwolves reporter Dane Moore reported Thursday that he has heard Minnesota is planning Garnett's jersey retirement for Feb. 28, when the Timberwolves host the Boston Celtics.

I've heard February 28th for the Kevin Garnett jersey retirement at Target Center.

The Wolves play the Boston Celtics that night.

— Dane Moore (@DaneMooreNBA) August 13, 2026

The Timberwolves have not formally announced the ceremony date. They previously confirmed that Garnett's number would be retired during the 2026-27 season, and the newly released schedule places Boston at Target Center that night.

Choosing the Celtics would connect the two defining chapters of Garnett's Hall of Fame career. Minnesota was where he grew up, became an MVP and gave a young franchise its identity. Boston was where he finally became an NBA champion.

The Celtics retired Garnett's No. 5 in March 2022. Nearly five years later, the number that belongs most deeply to Minnesota could join it in basketball immortality.

Getty Former Minnesota Timberwolves player Kevin Garnett is introduced before the start of the game between the New Orleans Pelicans and Minnesota Timberwolves at Target Center on April 12, 2026 in Minneapolis, Minnesota.

Few jersey retirements have been more obvious or more complicated.

Garnett remains the greatest player in Timberwolves history, leading the franchise in points, rebounds, assists, steals, blocks, games and minutes. Minnesota selected him fifth overall in the 1995 NBA draft, making him the first player in 20 years to jump directly from high school to the league.

He led the Wolves to eight consecutive playoff appearances and carried them to the 2004 Western Conference Finals after winning the league's MVP award. No Minnesota player before or since has matched his combination of production, intensity and connection with the fan base.

Yet his No. 21 remained absent from the rafters because of Garnett's fractured relationship with former Timberwolves owner Glen Taylor. Garnett stayed away from the organization after retiring in 2016, even as supporters repeatedly called for the franchise to honor him.

The ownership transfer to Marc Lore and Alex Rodriguez cleared the obstruction. After they completed their purchase from Taylor in 2025, Garnett returned as a Timberwolves and Lynx ambassador and rebuilt his connection to the franchise.

"I'm thrilled to be back home," Garnett said when the reunion was announced. "Minnesota is where it all began, where I was young, hungry and learning how to compete at the highest level."

The reconciliation became public in April, when Garnett attended a Wolves home game for the first time since 2018. He entered Target Center alongside Lore and Rodriguez and received the kind of reception that made the unfinished business impossible to ignore.

Now the franchise can complete the reunion against the team that benefited most from Minnesota's painful decision to trade him.

Garnett joined Boston in 2007 and immediately helped transform the Celtics into champions, winning Defensive Player of the Year during their 2007-08 title season. He spent six seasons there before later returning to Minnesota to close his career.

Boston owns No. 5, but No. 21 belongs to Minnesota. It represents the bark before tipoff, the powder tossed into the air, the Western Conference Finals run and an era when Garnett made the Timberwolves matter every night.

If Feb. 28 becomes official, Target Center will not simply honor the best player in franchise history. Minnesota will finally put its most important basketball memory where it has always belonged.

title: Brewers dealing with another injury during slump as Brice Turang is out
description: The Brewers are without their starting double play duo to begin a big four-game series at Dodger Stadium
fullText:
LOS ANGELES – With Cooper Pratt already on the shelf, the Milwaukee Brewers double-play combination took another hit before a critical series.

Second baseman Brice Turang was out of the lineup for the series opener Aug. 13 against the Los Angeles Dodgers at Dodger Stadium while dealing with left knee pain. Turang is day-to-day, manager Pat Murphy indicated, after an MRI didn't reveal any serious damage.

Turang will get a second opinion on the imaging.

"Been nursing this knee pain and just got to a point where he really needs to take some time," Murphy said. "We don't know how long. They're saying day-to-day. He had an MRI today. The MRI did not reveal so far anything we're too worried about. Obviously, he can't play tonight."

Turang, who is batting .268 with a .810 OPS and leads the team in runs and RBI, isn't yet ruled out for the four-game series between the top two teams in the National League.

Pratt, the Brewers starting shortstop, is on the 10-day injured list while Jackson Chourio, batting leadoff in the opener, continues to play through a left thumb injury. It's not an optimal situation coming off a three-game sweep in San Diego.

"A lot of things are hard right now but guess what?" Murphy said.

With the starting middle infield duo out, the Brewers got creative with their lineup against the Dodgers in the opener, playing Gary Sánchez at first base and Andrew Vaughn at third.

"Gary's a baseball player and we just keep putting baseball players out there," Murphy said. "Vaughn at third, Gary at first is not ideal. It doesn't show up on the metrics as this is going to be a great defensive team out there. Gary's a baseball player and his bat, how do we keep him out of there? And how do you get William [Contreras] going if you don't put him in there? That's the dilemma I'm in. With the middle infield out, it's tough."

title: Kevin Durant Pens Heartfelt Tribute After Russell Westbrook’s Retirement
description: Houston Rockets star Kevin Durant wrote a heartfelt tribute to Russell Westbrook on Thursday after his longtime teammate announced his retirement.Durant and Westbrook spent eight seasons together with the Oklahoma City Thunder and helped define an exciting era of NBA hoops. During his emotional farewell to his fellow MVP winner and scoring champion, Durant reflected […] The post Kevin Durant Pens Heartfelt Tribute After Russell Westbrook’s Retirement appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
Houston Rockets star Kevin Durant wrote a heartfelt tribute to Russell Westbrook on Thursday after his longtime teammate announced his retirement.

Durant and Westbrook spent eight seasons together with the Oklahoma City Thunder and helped define an exciting era of NBA hoops. During his emotional farewell to his fellow MVP winner and scoring champion, Durant reflected fondly upon the bond and journey the two NBA icons share.

GettyRussell Westbrook and Kevin Durant were teammates for eight seasons

On Thursday, Durant wrote a lengthy message on social media recalling Westbrook's tenacity, work ethic and influence.

The full transcript of his heartfelt tribute is as follows:

"I remember asking assistant coach Mo Cheeks, what's harder to do? Workout after practice or before?? I only asked cuz by time I would get to the gym, Russ was already done in the morning and I usually got mine in after practice. Mo like, 'coming in before practice is probably harder.' Since then, it's been my routine."

"A lot of people looked at the emotions on the court and thought Russ was loud. Nah, to me, he was quiet and methodical. He led by example, and once the lights were bright, he let everything out and experienced pure freedom. It was inspiring as his teammate. Everywhere I went, I saw it inspire people from all walks of life. Crazy thing is, he didn't say much; he just showed up. For 18 years."

Durant continued by wishing Westbrook well in his post-retirement life.

"This basketball life is sacred to us as professionals; what we put into that court means everything. Some of us wish we could go back and do things with a little more intent. Some can just wipe their hands and be satisfied with the time spent. Who u gonna be? We know what zero was on. Keep inspiring in the next phase of life, champ."

"I don't care what happens, can't erase what it was. The first YNs, finals run in our early 20s, All-Star games, seeing each other get injured and bounce back, the bus rides, plane rides, card games, jokes and arguments, the whole thing, memorable!!"

Durant concluded, "To the whole Westbrook family, Nina, the kids, mama Westbrook, big Russ, Ray, Donnell, everybody from Luezinger High and UCLA and many more that I'm forgettin, much love and Congratulations on an iconic career."

GettyRussell Westbrook is a two-time scoring champion and MVP winner

As Durant pointed out, Westbrook's legacy can never be understated or diminished.

Westbrook is one of the most decorated stars in NBA history and will be remembered by his immense passion and production on the floor.

During his storied NBA career, Westbrook earned nine All-Star and All-NBA selections. The dynamic guard was a two-time scoring champion and a three-time assists champion.

Westbrook has an NBA-record 209 triple-doubles. In those 209 such games, his teams had a cumulative record of 153-56.

Westbrook was named the 2016-17 NBA Most Valuable Player. He is also a member of the NBA 75th Anniversary Team.

title: Michigan quarterback Bryce Underwood downplays Ohio State rivalry
description: The most recent quote nugget from Michigan quarterback Bryce Underwood comes as a softening of the 'The Game' against Ohio State.
fullText:
"The Game." There has been much written about the Ohio State vs. Michigan football rivalry, and there will be plenty written about it in the future as well. There is also ink dedicated to one of the best rivalries in all of sports in the present as well, because of where things stand between the two ancient rivals and because of the changing of the guard at the head coaching position at Michigan.

New head coach Kyle Whittingham raised a lot of eyebrows by saying that there doesn't need to be hate between the two schools in order to win the annual grudge match, and now his quarterback, Bryce Underwood, is getting lit up for his comments about all things scarlet and gray.

While appearing in an interview with NBC Sports' John Fanta, Underwood, who had a very uninspiring game against the Buckeyes in Ann Arbor last season, was asked what makes 'The Game' different than any other. His answer -- well, it was a bit peculiar, seeing how many coaches have been fired on both sides because of the inability to do well on a Saturday in late November.

"It's just another game with guys in a different color," Underwood said. "That's how I see it."

Unfortunately for Underwood, that's not how most everyone else sees it. Former Michigan coach Jim Harbaugh nearly lost his job for his shortcomings against Urban Meyer and famously said the program "would die trying" to beat the Buckeyes, then turned it around (ahem -- in one way or another) to be glorified by Michigan fans. John Cooper, who had a stellar record otherwise, lost his job, by and large, for his 2-10-1 performance against the maize and blue. Guys have won the Heisman off the back of "The game," and fights have broken out, most famously at the end of the 2024 game in Columbus after an unranked Michigan team knocked off a heavily favored Ohio State squad that went on to win the College Football Playoff national championship.

Underwood went on to give plenty of other answers that seemed to downplay what a win against the Buckeyes means to many, saying that he just wants to be "1-0 every day" no matter who they are playing, and that "I lost, that's all it is" when asked about what went wrong against OSU last season. He also called it "a blessing" to play in The Game, and called it a "very physical" game earlier in the interview, but that won't play to anyone with a maize and blue wardrobe if Michigan and Underwood fail to deliver again this fall.

In some ways, it makes sense to downplay the biggest game of the year based on Underwood's 8-of-18 performance for just 63 yards, no touchdowns, and one interception. I'm no psychologist, but making things out to be not as important likely plays into a mindset for this year. However, with his comments and with what Whittingham said, it definitely feels like a different way of doing things for the cold, gray game against Michigan and Ohio State moving forward.

We'll see how it all plays out on November 28 in Columbus.

title: Liam Coen Says Jaguars 'Will Never be Able to Replace' Etienne
description: Following Travis Etienne’s departure to New Orleans, coach Liam Coen talked about what he brought to the Jaguars and how difficult he will be to replace.
fullText:
One of the biggest questions facing the Jacksonville Jaguars this season is how they will be able to replace running back Travis Etienne Jr.

Etienne had a great season in 2025 and was a big reason for the Jaguars winning 13 games. In his fifth season with Jacksonville, Etienne rushed for over 1,100 yards and scored 13 combined rushing and receiving touchdowns. He cashed in on his bounce-back year with a four-year contract from the New Orleans Saints in free agency.

Jacksonville is rolling with the duo of Bhayshul Tuten and its own free agent signing, Chris Rodriguez Jr., to fill the void left by Etienne. Tuten has looked great all offseason, flashing star potential. Rodriguez, who was sidelined with an injury during OTAs and minicamp, has been impressive since his return to practice at training camp. The bruiser has made the battle for RB1 a real competition, with the Jaguars still not naming a starter on the team's first depth chart.

With the Jaguars having two days of joint practices with Etienne and the Saints as the teams prepare to open the preseason against each other on Saturday, Jacksonville's head coach, Liam Coen, spoke about Etienne and how the team will be able to replace him.

For Coen, the answer is simple. He told reporters, as shared by Action Sports Jax, that the Jaguars won't be able to replace Etienne.

"We'll never be able to replace what he was able to do for us, whether it was last year or what he's done in Jacksonville throughout the course of his career," Coen admitted.

Etienne came to Jacksonville in 2021 after the Jaguars used their second first-round pick on him, reuniting the running back with his Clemson teammate, Trevor Lawrence, who was selected first overall.

A serious Lisfranc injury suffered during the preseason cost Etienne his entire rookie year. In the four seasons since, Etienne has rushed for 3,798 yards, with three 1,000-yard seasons and 25 touchdowns. He has added 1,338 receiving yards and 13 more scores through the air, including six in 2025.

Coen certainly thinks highly of Etienne and is happy to see him earn a big payday from his hometown team. But is he right about not being able to replace Etienne on the field?

The Jaguars' decision to go with a combination of Tuten and Rodriguez at running back has been criticized all offseason. The offense was sixth in the league in scoring last season, at 27.9 points per game. Many believe that, without Etienne, Jacksonville's offense will take a step back this season.

Despite the offense's success, the Jaguars finished 20th in the NFL last season with 115.1 rushing yards per game and averaged only a modest 4.0 yards per carry. They also did not fare well in rushing success rate in 2025, even during their 8-game winning streak to end the season.

Even with Etienne having a successful campaign, the Jaguars' running game has a lot of room to improve in 2026. Tuten, though he didn't show it much last year, is an explosive runner with breakaway speed. Rodriguez brings a power element to Jacksonville's backfield that the team has been lacking.

The duo of Tuten and Rodriguez, combined with second-year back LeQuint Allen Jr.'s receiving threat, should be able to replace Etienne's production this season.

Coen and the Jaguars' players are clearly happy to have a chance to catch up with their former teammate, and are happy he has found a new home in New Orleans.

Etienne brought a lot to Jacksonville during his time with the Jaguars, and he was a big part of the team's resurgence last season. However, Jacksonville's current stable of RBs all bring different skills to the table and should be able to form a successful backfield.

That takes nothing away from what Etienne accomplished during his time with the team, and he will be remembered as an important player in the Jaguars' history.

title: NBA schedule release: Winners & losers, including rookies, monster slates and some questionable decisions
description: Let's take stock of how things shook out on the day when every fanbase learned what lies ahead.
fullText:
The time has come. The NBA has officially dropped its 2026-27 regular-season schedule. As with anything in life, there are winners and losers — let's dive in.

Look, I'm a big fan of a good social media product. Russell Westbrook called it quits on a fruitful 18-year career and did so with aplomb, a beautifully crafted mini-movie highlighting all the best parts of his time in the NBA.

I'm also a fan of removing all of the pomp and circumstance and getting right to brass tacks with a schedule release, as well. And who better to do this with than Suns wing Dillon Brooks? Phoenix's social-media release was a hilarious breath of fresh air, a reminder that, yes, all 30 teams in fact do play against each other. Brooks, who looks anything but camera-ready, balls up the script, throws it at the camera and declares, "We play everyone," before staring directly at the camera in a manner similar to his trademark pregame ritual. It's obvious. It's brilliant.

2026-27 Phoenix Suns Schedule Release ft. The Villain 😈

📅: https://t.co/3xzH6RpMDP pic.twitter.com/xiZwZ2WzDA

I'm sure most of you are familiar with comedians/actors Keegan Michael-Key and Jordan Peele, and their old hit sketch comedy show, "Key & Peele." If not, get hip to it. For those that do remember the series, you'll immediately recall the infamous Substitute Teacher skit, featuring an enraged Key charged with taking attendance of his class. The only issue is Key is unable to pronounce anyone's name.

Introducing the Dallas Mavericks' social-media schedule release. Adding current players Dereck Lively and Max Christie to the scene — with some of the students wearing opponent team gear — was the icing on the cake in their homage to the original. Bravo.

2026-27 schedule? Here 🙋‍♀️🙋‍♂️@Ticketmaster // #MFFL pic.twitter.com/JX8umoe62J

It's one thing for the league to pivot to an earlier start time (much earlier) to kick off the regular season. But you can't have the reason you do — which involves the European market and its prime-time viewing slot — and present the international basketball fanbase with Celtics-Pistons. No disrespect to either franchise, both of whom won 56-plus games last season. But surely there could have been a bigger draw, with some actual European stars.

If the NBA truly wanted to capitalize on that day and bring in as many eyes as possible, there are better routes to take. Let's remove the current ring night from this equation temporarily. (I certainly understand the geographic storylines between the 76ers and Knicks.) But the fun in ring night comes in the opposing team waltzing in, not giving a crap about the reigning champs being crowned and raining on their parade. Concerning the Knicks, is there a better candidate out there than the Indiana Pacers? Not only do you get to highlight the return of star point guard Tyrese Haliburton, but you also re-ignite an actual rivalry.

I'm also not saying Philadelphia shouldn't be included, it absolutely should. But why not pit it against Boston? Can't think of a better emotionally slanted slate than seeing Jaylen Brown and Jayson Tatum square off after years of battles together. No one asked, but here's my ideal schedule:

Since there are so many different mouths the NBA has to feed concerning streaming rights, we're forced to follow a fragmented viewing experience. Nothing better than getting off after work, heading over to the local bar to wind down and asking the employees if any of the TVs have Peacock or Amazon Prime.

I love when teams have a good pulse on what's making waves for its schedule release. The name is Samuel Henderson, probably the best birdcaller I've ever seen (not a long list). Look him up. And then watch this.

The schedule is (bird) calling 🗣️ pic.twitter.com/FEItKvFPFr

Because of the structure of the NBA Cup, only eight teams will advance from the group stage to knockout play. Six winners from both conferences and two wild cards. This means there could potentially be five teams from this pool to be eliminated from the tournament.

Knicks. Cavs. 76ers. Pacers. Heat. Pacers. Something about that just feels cruel.

I'm pleased with the league's decision to move the latter stages of the competition out of Vegas — once a year is enough for the common man or woman — but why not Seattle or another city that doesn't currently have an NBA franchise? It feels like a missed opportunity playing at Hinkle Fieldhouse in Indianapolis.

With all the attention on the national television schedule, League Pass lovers might not be feeling attended to right now. I would ask that you look under your seats and pull out the piece of paper that says 11/2 on it. A quick run through some of the games …

Pistons-Hornets: Chess match featuring two of the games' brightest coaches.

Hawks-Pacers: East playoff teams are always a vibe.

Nets-Knicks: Battle of NY, featuring Julius Randle.

Wizards-Magic: I expect Washington to be competitive from the jump and all signs from Orlando indicate it has something to prove.

Celtics-Rockets: Ime Udoka's old friends, Tatum vs. Kevin Durant, possibly high-level playoff teams.

Jazz-Spurs: Victor Wembanyama against Utah's frontline should be a real treat.

Suns-Warriors: Steph Curry and Draymond Green dealing with a pesky Brooks (and Devin Booker/Jalen Green as a nice aside).

Raptors-Clippers: Which team will Kawhi be suiting up for? Legit question these days.

Heat-Lakers: Luka Dončić. Giannis Antetokounmpo. Downtown Los Angeles. Need I say more?

AJ Dybantsa (No. 1 pick) and Darryn Peterson (No. 2 pick) won't meet until the second to last day in February, well after the All-Star break. I was in the building for their first matchup in Vegas during Summer League, and the energy in the building was palpable. It's a shame we have to wait that long for a rematch.

Cam Boozer, the No. 3 pick (and my sleeper for the actual award) won't get any national TV time against either of his colleagues. If the NBA is all for promoting its young and upcoming stars, well, this is certainly one way to do it.

title: Liberty's Satou Sabally stepping away from team while continuing to recover from head injury
description: Sabally has suffered two concussions in the past year and hasn't appeared in a game since June 23.
fullText:
New York Liberty forward Satou Sabally will "be away from the team for a little bit," head coach Chris DeMarco told reporters before Thursday's game versus the Los Angeles Sparks.

"She's going to be away from the team for a little bit," DeMarco said, via the New York Post's Madeline Kenney. "It's her second significant head injury in the past 12 months. So, as with all our players, health will always be the focus, and we look forward to getting her back. She's just going to take some time right now."

While Sabally cleared concussion protocol, she was still feeling effects of the injury. On the WNBA injury report, her status changed from "concussion protocol" to "head injury" on Wednesday.

Sabally, 28, hasn't played since June 23 while recovering from a concussion sustained in an 87-76 win over the Las Vegas Aces. During the first quarter, she was hit in the face by an elbow from NaLyssa Smith while the two were going for a rebound.

The seven-year veteran fell to the court, but eventually got up without assistance and came out of the game. She returned in the second quarter, but left again after playing four minutes and did not reenter the game.

High low passing ✔️

Han Xu whips it to Satou Sabally for the easy score

IND-NYL | CBS & Paramount+ | 2026 WNBA Commissioner’s Cup | @coinbase 
Tap to watch: https://t.co/MJPIwIY5N0 pic.twitter.com/He0zVvIDHz

As DeMarco mentioned, that was the second concussion Sabally has suffered in the past year. During Game 3 of the WNBA Finals with the Phoenix Mercury, Sabally collided with Aces defender Kierstan Bell with her head hitting Bell's knee. Sabally continued experiencing concussion symptoms, which kept her from playing in Unrivaled's second season with Phantom BC.

DeMarco did not offer a timetable for when Sabally could return, saying, "We'll get there."

"This is under the guidance of our performance team," he added, via the Post. "But just for now, she's just taking some time away, making sure she's healthy."

In 13 games this season (five starts) with the Liberty, Sabally has averaged 10.4 points and 2.8 rebounds, far below her career averages. During her seven seasons, she has scored 15.4 points per game while grabbing 6.4 rebounds and dishing out 3.2 assists. Sabally signed a two-year, $1.67 million contract with New York before this season.

After Thursday's game, the Liberty have nine games remaining on their regular-season schedule. At 20-14, they are currently tied with the Dallas Wings for the seventh seed in the WNBA standings and are virtually assured of making the playoffs. New York could still finish as high as third or get the league's final postseason berth in eighth place.

title: Mike Vrabel reveals real reason Christian Gonzalez missed practice
description: Patriots coach Mike Vrabel broke his silence on star cornerback Christian Gonzalez's absence from the team's joint training camp practice.
fullText:
One of the biggest headlines for the New England Patriots this week has been star cornerback Christian Gonzalez's absence from Tuesday's joint training camp practice with the Indianapolis Colts.

Some wondered if he skipped the practice due to his ongoing contract situation. With the intensity increasing for the scrimmage, perhaps Gonzalez finally decided enough was enough and held out of participating.

However, ESPN's Mike Reiss pointed to another possibility. At the end of Monday's practice, there was a play in the end zone where Gonzalez looked like he might have been injured while attempting to guard veteran receiver Romeo Doubs.

In a pregame interview with 98.5 The Sports Hub on Thursday, via Boston Herald's Zack Cox, Vrabel confirmed the injury was the reason why Gonzalez didn't practice.

"Everybody that was healthy practiced (Tuesday)," Vrabel said. "So those guys, we didn't deem them healthy enough to go out there and participate. When they're ready, they'll be back out there. I feel like they've all tried to start camp with their own purpose. Gonzo came out competitive and practiced and, I thought, improved. As good as he is, he knows he can still improve."

Vrabel's reasoning makes sense considering Gonzalez has been a full participant throughout training camp, despite his ongoing contract negotiations.

Granted, the Patriots are hoping to get a deal done sooner rather than later, but they are also hoping to have their star defender available to them for the 2026 season.

title: Returning Rockford Boylan players are convinced they can bounce back this season
description: Boylan High School very rarely goes through head coaching changes, but the Titans are this year. Joel Beard is the guy now, a coach with a lot of college coaching experience in his background at the junior college level.
fullText:
ROCKFORD, Ill. (WTVO/WQRF) — Boylan High School very rarely goes through head coaching changes, but the Titans are this year. Joel Beard is the guy now, a coach with a lot of college coaching experience in his background at the junior college level.

There are two things that we do know about Beard already. He is fired up to be coaching the Titans, and he's known for overseeing explosive, high-scoring offenses in the past at the College of DuPage. That's the type of offense he ultimately wants to have at Boylan.

"We like to be explosive. Make some explosive plays and get everybody involved. We like to be multiple that way and keep defenses guessing."

"He's working us really hard," said Boylan senior linebacker/tight end Nick Polivka of his new head coach. "This is going to be my fourth year, and this is probably the hardest summer since I've been here. I'm really excited."

The coaching change from former coach John Cacciatore to Beard, and a 2-7 season last year for Boylan, led to several key players transferring to other NIC-10 schools. The Titans are ready to roll though with who they have, and they believe there's more than enough talent here to have a bounce-back season.

"We're going to rock with who we've got," said Polivka. "We've got, I think, the best guys. I'm very confident in our team with what we've got going."

Polivka is part of a linebacker unit that should be very strong. Eyzaiah Campos will be one of the other outside linebackers, and in the middle will be junior Keaton Hampl. He missed some time last year with an injury. Hampl is ready to roll. He has the size and aggressiveness to be a beast.

"He's going to anchor our defense," said Bear.

"It feels great to be out here 100 percent," said Hampl who missed most of last season with an injury."

The Titans also have an experienced safety in Henry Maier, and a couple linemen up front who will be impact players on defense, Erick Becerra and Edy Espinoza.

On offense, senior Michael Davenport takes over at quarterback. He has some good targets in Jake Fowler and athletic receiver Mikele Sims. Basketball has been Sims' sport, but now he is giving football a shot, and he looks like he could be one of those explosive playmakers that Beard wants.

When the Titans run the ball, Sam Bland and Campos will be doing most of the work. Espinoza, Becerra, Peyton Kirchner and Caleb Gork will provide the blocking up front.

title: Will Shohei Ohtani pitch soon? Dave Roberts provides update on Dodgers star
description: Shohei Ohtani, who made his last start on the mound July 3, has been playing catch and potentially will throw a bullpen session soon.
fullText:
LOS ANGELES — Dodgers manager Dave Roberts provided some encouraging news, if only a glimmer of it, regarding Shohei Ohtani's ability to resume pitching.

"He's playing catch, potentially going to throw a bullpen soon,'' Roberts told the media before the Dodgers opened their four-game homestand with the Milwaukee Brewers Thursday, Aug. 13.

Though the Dodgers have indicated they expect Ohtani to pitch again this season, the team has offered no timeline. It would be most critical to get him back when the playoffs start.

Ohtani hasn't pitched since July 3 because of inflammation in his left knee. He'd been brilliant on the mound until the knee issue surfaced.

The knee problem hasn't kept Ohtani out of the lineup as the team's designated hitter. He leads the Dodgers with 26 home runs, a slugging percentage of .544 and an on-base percentage of .393.

Roberts indicated he expects Ohtani to play all four games against the Brewers and will evaluate him before the Dodgers start a three-game series at Colorado Aug. 17.

title: Nolan Wells’ family still hasn’t turned over phone: Attorney
description: Wells went missing over the July 4 weekend when he and a group of friends traveled by boat to an island off the Mississippi coast.
fullText:
(NewsNation) — More than five weeks after the mysterious death of Nolan Wells, the Mississippi teen's family reportedly has not handed over his cell phone for a joint digital examination, but a legal representative says there's nothing amiss.

Ahmad Smith, one of the attorneys representing the Wells family, said his clients remain willing to finalize details with authorities to conduct the forensic examination.

"To the extent there has been any suggestion that we have been unwilling or have failed to cooperate with the investigation, we want to make clear that this is not the case," Smith said in a letter to prosecutors this week.

His statement follows comments from Tyler Cox, the attorney representing three friends of Wells.

Cox told SiriusXM host Dan Abrams on Monday the family has yet to turn over their son's phone after publicly alleging some data may have been deleted.

"I have reason to believe, and I do believe, that (Wells' family) have not cooperated with law enforcement. I do not think that they have turned in Nolan's phone, and I'm willing to bet my reputation on that. I don't think they've cooperated at all," Cox said.

Wells, 18, went missing over the July 4 weekend when he and a group of friends traveled by boat to Horn Island off the Mississippi coast.

The friends had his phone when they returned and gave it to Wells' family members.

The teen's body was found July 6. Results of a state autopsy have not been released, and a second autopsy performed by pathologist Roger Mitchell is inconclusive, pending more information.

Smith's letter asks prosecutors to help Mitchell get access to materials from the first autopsy. State medical examiners kept portions of Wells' body for further study, which experts say is not unusual.

title: 'Big Short' investor Steve Eisman says Anthropic and OpenAI are the 'Achilles' heel' of the AI trade
description: The veteran of the 2008 market crash is concerned that the success so many companies is reliant on the fortunes of just two AI labs.
fullText:
Steve Eisman is worried that success of the AI trade relies on just two companies: OpenAI and Anthropic.

The famed investor warns of risks to the broader AI ecosystem if they were to run into trouble.

A price war with cheaper Chinese models would be a problem for OpenAI and Anthropic, he says.

The market is eagerly awaiting the day when OpenAI and Anthropic go public, but to Steve Eisman, the two AI giants are the soft underbelly of the AI trade.

Anthropic is barreling toward an IPO that could surpass this summer's historic SpaceX offering by valuation and by funds raised. Reports of a $2 trillion valuation would vault the Claude maker into the ranks of the world's most valuable companies.

But Steve Eisman, the trader whose contrarian bets against the housing market were chronicled in "The Big Short," is worried that too much of the AI trade is reliant on the success of just two companies.

"The 'Achilles' heel' of this whole story, if there's going to be an Achilles' heel, is if something bad happens to Anthropic and OpenAI," Eisman told CNBC, warning of a potential price war if cheaper models from China start to take market share. "And then we have a problem."

After years of powering stocks to new highs, the AI trade has proven to be a market-driving force yet again in 2026, concerns about the sustainability of the investment boom continue to grow.

"The issue is, to me, that something like 70% of all AI revenue from Microsoft, Amazon, Google, Oracle is from Anthropic and OpenAI. Period. Just those two…The futures of these massive companies, in a sense, are a bet that OpenAI Anthropic are going to succeed."

Eisman isn't the first to raise concerns about the finances of the two AI giants. Researcher and independent journalist Ed Zitron warned earlier this summer that OpenAI could end up being the Lehman Brothers of the AI trade, a systemic risk that takes down other companies if it were to stumble.

Meanwhile, the rise of the open-weight Chinese models, such as Kimi K3, caused panic on Wall Street last month as chip stocks fell on fears greater competition in the AI market. But as with DeepSeek's roll out in January 2025, the losses have mostly been recovered and the jitters have subsisded. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index is up 75% year to date.

Despite his concerns, Eisman clarified that he's not willing to make a call on a price war between OpenAI and Anthropic and their Chinese rivals yet, at least not until investors have more information about both companies' finances.

"It'll be nice when Anthropic goes public, so we can see real numbers and then see every quarter how they're doing," he stated. "Until then, it's just anecdotal."
